mainTopic: The source for the seven-day separation of the כהן גדול before יום כיפור (and of the כהן who burns the פרה אדומה): the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן, who learns it from the מילואים, and ריש לקיש, who learns it from סיני.
overview: This amud opens with the last words of the previous discussion: the כהן גדול is moved out of his home because of possible impurity from his wife. Then רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש. A ברייתא says the כהן is sprinkled all seven days. That fits the מילואים, where there was sprinkling, but there was no sprinkling at סיני. ריש לקיש counters that the מילואים used blood, not water. רבי יוחנן answers with רבי חייא's teaching that water replaced blood, and ריש לקיש finally says the sprinkling is only a מעלה. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן. It reads 'בזאת יבא אהרן' as pointing to the מילואים and adds the פסוק 'כאשר עשה ביום הזה'. The גמרא explains why the feminine 'בזאת' teaches two things, and why the second פסוק was needed: it shows the separation applies to every יום הכפורים and every כהן גדול. Last, a ברייתא supporting ריש לקיש describes משה being set apart in the cloud at סיני, following רבי יוסי הגלילי's timeline. רבי עקיבא disagrees and says those days began on ראש חודש.

steps.title: Closing words: concern for the impurity of his household
steps.stepSummary: These are the final words of a statement earlier. They explain that the separation is out of concern for impurity coming from the כהן's home, meaning his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...because of the impurity of his household (his wife).
steps.whatsHappening: This short phrase finishes a thought that began on the previous amud. It gives the reason the כהן is moved out of his home: concern about impurity from his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his wife turned out to be a נדה and he had relations with her, he would become טמא for seven days. Taking him out of his house for the week protects him from that seven-day impurity. The next steps return to the main question of where the seven-day separation comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: the impurity of his 'house', a polite way of referring to his wife

phrases.english: for the impurity of his household.
phrases.notes: This finishes the line from before; 'his household' here means his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement that began earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The separation from his home guards against the seven-day impurity that could come from his wife.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a ברייתא about sprinkling the כהן all seven days fits his source (the מילואים), but does not fit ריש לקיש's source (סיני), since nobody was sprinkled at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to ריש לקיש: According to me, since I learn this from the מילואים, I can explain the ברייתא. It says that both the כהן who burns the פרה and the כהן גדול before יום כיפור are sprinkled all seven days with ashes from all the earlier פרות. That is because there was also sprinkling at the מילואים. But according to you, since you learn it from סיני, was there any sprinkling at סיני?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן uses a known ברייתא to attack ריש לקיש's view. The ברייתא matches his own source but seems to have no match at סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seven days are modeled on an earlier event, their details should match that event. At the מילואים, משה sprinkled on אהרן and his sons. So a week that includes sprinkling makes sense if it is modeled on the מילואים. At סיני there was no sprinkling, so ריש לקיש's model cannot explain where the sprinkling comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: 'granted' or 'it works out', the opening of a 'this fits my view, but not yours' challenge
the seven days when the מִשְׁכָּן and the כֹּהֲנִים were inaugurated
they sprinkle on him (purifying water)
here: the ashes of earlier פָּרוֹת אֲדֻמּוֹת, which the תּוֹרָה calls a חַטָּאת
sprinkling

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חטאות' does not mean regular sin-offerings. It means the ashes of earlier פרות אדומות that were kept in the מקדש.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to Reish Lakish:
Granted, according to me, since I derive it from the inauguration,
that explains what was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה וְזֶה מַזִּין עָלָיו כׇּל שִׁבְעָה
phrases.english: for both this one and that one, they sprinkle on him all seven days
from all the red heifer ashes that were kept there,
because there was also sprinkling at the inauguration.
But according to you, since you derive it from Sinai,
was there sprinkling at Sinai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the debate over the source of the seven-day separation.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the seven-day separation is learned from סיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires sprinkling during the seven days. That matches the מילואים but has no parallel at סיני.

steps.title: ריש לקיש counters: blood versus water
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers with a challenge of his own: even for רבי יוחנן the match is not exact, since the מילואים used blood and here the sprinkling is with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And according to your reasoning, does it fit? At the מילואים it was blood; here it is water!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש does not answer directly. He shows that רבי יוחנן's own model has a similar weakness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the מילואים, משה sprinkled blood of the קרבנות on אהרן. Before יום כיפור, the כהן is sprinkled with water mixed with פרה ashes. So the 'sprinkling' parallel is not exact for רבי יוחנן either.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and according to your own reasoning', turning a challenge back on the challenger
does it work out well?

phrases.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning, does it work out?
At the inauguration it was blood; here it is water!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי יוחנן's challenge with a counter-challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the sprinkling matches the מילואים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The material is different (blood versus water), so the parallel fails.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answers: water replaced blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers using רבי חייא's teaching that water takes the place of blood, so the parallel still holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult, because רבי חייא taught: Water took the place of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends his view against ריש לקיש's counter-challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important point is the act of sprinkling, not the exact material. Since water was set up as a replacement for blood, sprinkling water still counts as matching the מילואים.

keyTerms.meaning: that is not a problem
water came in place of blood

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
for Rabbi Chiya taught:
Water entered in place of blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, דְּתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Substitution: water serves as a replacement for blood.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A different material would break the parallel to the מילואים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Water is a recognized replacement for blood, so the sprinkling still matches the מילואים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן repeats his challenge
steps.stepSummary: Having defended himself, רבי יוחנן asks his original question again: according to ריש לקיש, was there any sprinkling at סיני?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to you, was there sprinkling at סיני?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings back his first question, since ריש לקיש has not yet answered it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's counter-challenge has been answered, so the burden is back on him. He still needs to explain the sprinkling, which has no source at סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: but according to you

phrases.english: But according to you,
was there sprinkling at Sinai?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְדִידָךְ, הַזָּאָה בְּסִינַי מִי הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering the counter-challenge, returns to the original question from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the source is סיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There was no sprinkling at סיני, so ריש לקיש cannot explain the sprinkling in the ברייתא.

steps.title: ריש לקיש answers: it is only an extra stringency
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the sprinkling is not derived from the source at all. It is just an added stringency set by the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is merely an added stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers by saying the sprinkling does not need a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The separation itself is learned from סיני. The sprinkling is an extra precaution that the חכמים added. Since it is not required by the source, it does not need a parallel at סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: merely an added stringency or precaution, not a core requirement

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן learns the seven days from the מילואים, and the sprinkling fits that source because water replaced blood. ריש לקיש learns them from סיני, and for him the sprinkling is just a מעלה.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is merely an added stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the repeated challenge from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification: the sprinkling is a rabbinic stringency, not part of the derived law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sprinkling must come from the same source as the seven-day separation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sprinkling is an extra stringency and needs no parallel at סיני.

steps.title: Each view has a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that there is a ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן and another supporting ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with רבי יוחנן, and a ברייתא was taught in line with ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to quote one ברייתא for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views turn out to have earlier תנאים behind them. This shows that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are continuing an older מחלוקת, not starting a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא was taught that agrees with him

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan,
a baraita was taught in accordance with Reish Lakish.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate itself to supporting sources for each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a ברייתא supporting each of the two views.

steps.title: The ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן: 'בזאת' points to the מילואים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads 'בזאת יבא אהרן אל הקדש' as 'with what is stated in this topic,' meaning the מילואים. There, אהרן separated for seven days while משה trained him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with רבי יוחנן: 'With this אהרן shall come into the holy place' means with what was said in the topic. What is that? The topic of the מילואים. And what is said in the topic of the מילואים? אהרן separated for seven days and served on one day, and משה taught him all seven days to train him in the עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first ברייתא, which supports רבי יוחנן by linking יום כיפור to the מילואים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בזאת' ('with this') is read as 'with what is stated in the topic', meaning the topic of the מילואים (ויקרא ח). During the מילואים, אהרן was set apart for seven days while משה trained him. So the כהן גדול before יום כיפור is likewise set apart for seven days to be trained, which is exactly רבי יוחנן's source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'with this אַהֲרֹן shall come into the holy place' (ויקרא טז:ג), the opening of the יום כיפור service
in the topic or section
separated or withdrew
to train him in the Temple service

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source behind the practice in the משנה of separating the כהן גדול for seven days and training him before יום כיפור.

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan:
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats this opening line so it can start quoting the actual ברייתא.

phrases.english: "With this Aaron shall come into the Sanctuary,"
meaning with what is stated in the topic,
what is it? The topic of the inauguration.
And what is stated in the topic of the inauguration?

phrases.aramaic: אַהֲרֹן פֵּירַשׁ שִׁבְעָה וְשִׁמֵּשׁ יוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Aaron withdrew for seven days and served one day,
and Moses transmitted to him all seven days
in order to train him in the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּזֹאת יָבֹא אַהֲרֹן אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the first half of the announcement in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that the seven-day separation is learned from the מילואים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads 'בזאת' (ויקרא טז:ג) as pointing to the topic of the מילואים, where אהרן separated seven days and was trained by משה.

steps.title: Every future כהן גדול also separates for seven days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: what happened at the מילואים applies for all generations. Every כהן גדול separates for seven days before יום הכפורים, and two real תלמידי חכמים train him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for all generations as well, the כהן גדול separates for seven days and serves on one day. Two תלמידי חכמים from the students of משה (not צדוקים) teach him all seven days, to train him in the עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא carries the מילואים model forward to every future יום הכפורים. Just as משה trained אהרן for seven days, scholars train each new כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 established the source: 'בזאת' points back to the מילואים. Here the ברייתא turns that history into a lasting rule: seven days of separation, then one day of service. It also adds that the trainers must be true students of משה, which excludes the צדוקים, who did not accept the חכמים's tradition about the יום הכפורים service.

keyTerms.meaning: For future generations; a permanent rule, not a one-time event
Separates or withdraws (from his home)
Sadducees, a sect that rejected the חכמים's oral tradition
To train him or initiate him

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'students of משה' does not mean people who lived in משה's time. It means scholars who follow משה's tradition, the תורה שבעל פה, as opposed to the צדוקים.

phrases.english: And for the generations as well,
the High Priest withdraws seven days
and serves one day.
And two Torah scholars
from among the students of Moshe,
to exclude Sadducees,
transmit the guidelines to him all seven days
in order to train him in the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף לְדוֹרוֹת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל פּוֹרֵשׁ שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 8, extending the מילואים precedent into a permanent rule.
steps.raayaObject: That the seven-day separation of the כהן גדול is derived from the מילואים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reading of 'בזאת יבא אהרן אל הקדש'.

steps.title: The ברייתא links its source to the משנה, including the פרה and the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that the משנה's rule comes from this source. The כהן גדול and the כהן who burns the פרה are both separated for seven days, and both are sprinkled all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: seven days before יום הכפורים, they move the כהן גדול from his house to the לשכת פרהדרין. Just as they separate the כהן גדול, they also separate the כהן who burns the פרה, to the chamber facing the בירה in the northeast. For both of them, they sprinkle on him all seven days from all the פרה אדומה ashes that were there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quotes the משנה's ruling and says it comes from the מילואים source just discussed. This is the part that matters for the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is that the פרה separation and the sprinkling are listed under 'מכאן אמרו', so they are presented as derived from the source. That fits רבי יוחנן, who learns both יום הכפורים and the פרה from the מילואים. It does not fit ריש לקיש's answer in Step 6, that the sprinkling is only a stringency of the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said; this source is the basis for the ruling
The Chamber of פרהדרין, where the כהן גדול stayed during his separation
The בירה, a name for the Temple area or a building on the Temple Mount
They sprinkle (the purifying water)
Here: the ashes of earlier פרות אדומות, which the תורה calls a חטאת

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is why the ברייתא counts as support for רבי יוחנן. It treats the פרה and the sprinkling as coming from the source itself.

phrases.english: From here they said:
Seven days before Yom Kippur
they remove the High Priest from his house
to the Chamber of Parhedrin.
And just as they remove the High Priest,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ מַפְרִישִׁין כֹּהֵן הַשּׂוֹרֵף אֶת הַפָּרָה
phrases.english: so they remove the priest who burns the heifer
to the chamber that faces the bira,
at the northeast.
And for both this one and that one,
they sprinkle on him all seven days
from all the sin-offerings (heifer ashes) that were there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the derived rule from Step 9 to the משנה, adding the פרה and the sprinkling.
steps.raayaObject: That the separation for the פרה and the sprinkling both come from the מילואים source, as רבי יוחנן holds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's 'מכאן אמרו' attached to the משנה's text.

steps.title: The ברייתא raises a problem: blood there, water here
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises its own objection. At the מילואים the sprinkling was with blood, but here it is with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: at the מילואים it was blood, and here it is water...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pauses to raise a problem with its own comparison. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sprinkling during the seven days is learned from the מילואים, the material should match. At the מילואים they sprinkled blood, but now they sprinkle פרה אדומה water. This is the same difficulty that was raised against רבי יוחנן earlier in the סוגיא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say; introduces an expected objection
The seven-day inauguration of the משכן and the כהנים

phrases.english: And if you say:
at the inauguration it was blood, here it is water,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison made in Step 10 between the מילואים sprinkling and today's sprinkling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between the מילואים sprinkling and the seven-day sprinkling of today.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The materials differ (blood versus water), so the comparison seems to fail.

steps.title: Water takes the place of blood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that water took the place of blood, so the comparison still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: You must say: water came in place of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The difference in material does not break the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly רבי חייא's teaching that רבי יוחנן used back in Step 4. Here the ברייתא states it in its own words, which gives רבי יוחנן's defense direct support from an earlier source.

keyTerms.meaning: Water came in place of blood; the water now does the job the blood once did

phrases.english: you must say: water came in place of blood.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Substitution: the new material fills the role of the old one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the materials differ, the sprinkling cannot be derived from the מילואים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Water replaced blood, so the comparison stands.

steps.title: A second פסוק links the מילואים to both the פרה and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings another פסוק from the מילואים. 'To do' refers to the פרה, and 'to atone' refers to יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'As was done on this day, so ה׳ commanded to do, to atone for you.' 'To do' means the actions of the פרה. 'To atone' means the actions of יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second proof that both the פרה and יום הכפורים follow the pattern of the מילואים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly רבי יוחנן's source from the start of the סוגיא. The פסוק at the מילואים is read as covering two future services: the פרה ('לעשות') and יום הכפורים ('לכפר'). That is why this ברייתא counts as support for רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And it says; introduces an additional פסוק as further proof
To do; here read as referring to the פרה אדומה
To atone; here read as referring to יום הכפורים

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן. Both the פרה and יום הכפורים are learned from the מילואים, and water stands in for blood.

phrases.english: And it says:
"As has been done this day,
so the Lord commanded to do, to make atonement for you."
"To do": these are the actions of the heifer;
"to atone": these are the actions of Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to strengthen the derivation, now that the blood-and-water objection has been answered.
steps.raayaObject: That both the פרה and יום הכפורים are derived from the מילואים, as רבי יוחנן holds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא ח:לד, 'כאשר עשה ביום הזה צוה ה׳ לעשות לכפר עליכם'.

steps.title: Isn't 'בזאת' needed for the offerings themselves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reading. The word 'בזאת' is needed for its plain meaning: אהרן enters with a bull for a חטאת and a ram for an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this word 'בזאת' is needed for its own plain meaning: with a young bull for a חטאת and a ram for an עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now examines the ברייתא and questions how it can use 'בזאת' to teach about separation at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, 'בזאת' introduces the offerings that אהרן brings. If the word is already doing that job, it seems it is not free to also teach about the seven-day separation.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for its own plain purpose
A young bull for a חטאת
A ram for an עולה

phrases.english: But this word "with this"
is needed for its own plain meaning:
with a young bull for a sin-offering
and a ram for a burnt-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the ברייתא's opening reading of 'בזאת' (Step 8) and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading of 'בזאת' as pointing to the מילואים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A word that is needed for its plain meaning cannot also be used for an extra teaching.

steps.title: The feminine form 'בזאת' teaches two things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if the word meant only the offerings, the תורה would have written 'בזה' or 'באלה'. The unusual 'בזאת' shows it teaches both the offerings and the separation.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: if it meant only the offerings, let the פסוק say 'בזה' or 'באלה'. Why 'בזאת'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge using the grammar of the word. The next step continues analyzing the same ברייתא, asking why it needed a second פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'פר' and 'איל' are masculine nouns, so 'בזה' (this) or 'באלה' (these) would fit them. The feminine 'בזאת' does not match either offering, so it must also point to something else: the topic of the מילואים, which teaches the separation. The word therefore teaches about the offerings and about the separation.

keyTerms.meaning: They say; introduces the answer of the חכמים
With this (masculine form)
With these (plural)
Learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: 'בזאת' teaches two things: the offerings of יום הכפורים, and the seven-day separation learned from the מילואים.

phrases.english: They say:
If it were for the offering alone,
let the verse say "with this" (masculine) or "with these,"
so what is the point of "bezot" (feminine)?
Learn two things from it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: the unusual word form shows a double teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בזאת' refers only to the offerings, so it cannot teach about the separation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The feminine 'בזאת' teaches both the offerings and the separation learned from the מילואים.

steps.title: Why did the ברייתא need a second פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא added 'ואומר' and brought another פסוק, when it already had a source.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא brought an extra פסוק. This question sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains what the first source might have missed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ואומר' means a second proof is being added. A second proof is only needed if the first one leaves a gap. The גמרא wants to find that gap.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says': a formula that adds a second פסוק as proof
What? Why?

phrases.english: What is 'and it says'? (Why add another verse?)
phrases.notes: He's asking why the ברייתא goes on to bring a second פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the source from 'בזאת' is settled, the גמרא asks why the ברייתא added another proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What gap in the first proof makes the second פסוק necessary?

steps.title: The second פסוק shows פרישה applies in every generation
steps.stepSummary: Without the extra פסוק, we might think only the first יום הכפורים, or only אהרן as the first כהן גדול, needed פרישה. 'כאשר עשה' teaches it applies forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say: only the first יום הכפורים needs separation, just like we find at the מילואים, but a regular יום הכפורים does not. Or you might say: only the first כהן גדול needs separation, but later כהנים גדולים do not. So come and hear: 'As He did on this day, so ה׳ commanded to do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The first source could be read as a one-time event, so the ברייתא added 'כאשר עשה' to show the rule is permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source from the מילואים might seem tied to that special first time. The גמרא suggests two possible limits: only the first יום הכפורים, or only the first כהן גדול. The words 'כאשר עשה ביום הזה צוה ה׳ לעשות' tell us that what was done then must be done again in all future years.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say: introduces a possible mistaken thought
The first
Separation: the כהן גדול's seven days away from his home before יום הכפורים
In general, regular (not the special first time)
Alternatively, or else
Come and hear: introduces a source that settles the issue

steps.whatToRemember: The second פסוק ('כאשר עשה') makes פרישה a rule for every יום הכפורים and every כהן גדול, not only a one-time event at the מילואים.

phrases.english: And if you would say: it is the first Yom Kippur
that requires separation
as we find at the inauguration
but on a regular Yom Kippur, no.
Alternatively: it is the first High Priest
who requires separation
but a High Priest in general, no.
Come and hear: 'As He did, etc.'
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא ח:לד: 'כאשר עשה ביום הזה צוה ה׳ לעשות', meaning it applies for all generations.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra פסוק rules out limiting פרישה to the first יום הכפורים or the first כהן גדול. It is a rule for all generations.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports ריש לקיש: משה was set apart in the cloud
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that משה went up, was covered, and was made holy in the cloud before receiving the תורה. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, these six days came after עשרת הדברות, which fits ריש לקיש's source for פרישה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that supports ריש לקיש: משה went up in the cloud, was covered in the cloud, and was made holy in the cloud, so that he could receive the תורה for ישראל in holiness. As it says: 'The glory of ה׳ rested on הר סיני.' This happened after עשרת הדברות, and those days were the start of the forty days. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports ריש לקיש, who learns the כהן גדול's פרישה from משה at הר סיני. משה spent six days covered by the cloud before ה׳ called him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said the source for פרישה is 'ויכסהו הענן ששת ימים', meaning משה waited six days before entering. רבי יוסי הגלילי says these six days came after עשרת הדברות and were the start of משה's forty days on the mountain. So the waiting was a special preparation for משה himself, which is exactly the model ריש לקיש needs.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in support of him
Cloud
Was made holy
'And the glory of ה׳ rested' (שמות כד:טז)
The Ten Commandments

steps.confusionAlert: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, the six days of the cloud are not the days of preparation before מתן תורה. He places them after עשרת הדברות, at the start of the forty days. רבי עקיבא disagrees in the next step and places them from ראש חודש, before עשרת הדברות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the כהן גדול's seven-day separation to משה's preparation at סיני, as ריש לקיש holds.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Reish Lakish:
Moses ascended in the cloud,
and was covered in the cloud,
and was sanctified in the cloud,
in order to receive the Torah for Israel in holiness,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּשְׁכּוֹן כְּבוֹד ה׳ עַל הַר סִינַי״ —
phrases.english: as it is stated: 'And the glory of the Lord rested on Mount Sinai'
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues: 'and the cloud covered him six days.'

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה אַחַר עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת,
phrases.english: this event was after the Ten Commandments,
and they (the six days) were the beginning of the forty days,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the analysis of the ברייתא on the מילואים (רבי יוחנן's side), the גמרא turns back to support ריש לקיש's source from סיני.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that the source for פרישה is משה's six days in the cloud at סיני
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (רבי יוסי הגלילי) teaching that משה was covered and sanctified in the cloud for six days after עשרת הדברות, before going up for forty days

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the six days began on ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. He holds that 'the glory of ה׳ rested' refers to the days starting from ראש חודש סיון, before עשרת הדברות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'And the glory of ה׳ rested' means from ראש חודש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a different timeline. He says the six days of the cloud started on ראש חודש סיון, before מתן תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the six days are the days leading up to עשרת הדברות, not a separate preparation for משה afterward. On his reading, the ברייתא does not clearly fit ריש לקיש's model of a special separation for משה before going up.

keyTerms.meaning: The first of the month (here, of סיון)

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
'And the glory of the Lord rested': from the New Moon.
phrases.notes: That is, from ראש חודש סיון, six days before עשרת הדברות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing reading of the same פסוק that רבי יוסי הגלילי explained in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The six days of the cloud began on ראש חודש סיון, before עשרת הדברות.
